lens: F6_Better_Alternative — What's the better way to do this? Why not that way? If 'later', is there a bounded FixupTask with priority + reasoning? Did the author consider at least one Linus-style and one hyperscaler-style alternative?
answer: PASS_WITH_RESERVATIONS. The four sub-checks (check_rust_default_language, check_naming_convention, check_scorecard_render, check_consensus_debate_evidence) all encode a 'Day-1 stub + bounded FixupTask' pattern that IS a defensible alternative-selection: each defers full enforcement to a NAMED FixupTask (F-LANE-RUST-DEFAULT-ENFORCE, F-NAMING-CONVENTION-ENFORCE, F-LANE-SCORECARD-RENDER, F-LANE-DEBATE-SUBCHECK), all four are registered in registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl with priority=medium + source_change_id + reasoning, and status=NotYetArmed surfaces the deferral honestly (no silent stubbing). However, the author did NOT visibly enumerate Linus-style ('walk a real Cargo metadata DAG / parse JSON properly with serde') or hyperscaler-style ('shell out to a sandboxed worker / event-stream the scan / arm a CI matrix per home') alternatives in code-comments or the FixupTask body. The 'better way' question is implicitly answered as 'land the FixupTask later' but NO inline rationale rejects competing day-1 implementations. The extract_string_field helper at L717-727 is a particularly clear first-solution-wins risk: hand-rolled scalar regex when serde_json was an option — the doc-comment cites F-LANE-SEAM-IMPL-FULL-JSON, so the deferral IS bounded, but no rejected-alternative reasoning is captured.
key_claims: All four new pub fn sub-checks have a corresponding registered FixupTask with priority=medium, source_session, source_change_id, and day1_result fields populated — the 'later' commitment is bounded, not hand-waved.
Status enum (Pass / Fail / NotYetArmed) is the alternative-selection seam: it makes the deferred-enforcement choice machine-readable and CI-visible rather than burying it in TODO comments.

Day-1 implementations all use std::fs::read_dir + substring matching (raw.contains("\"meta_review_triggered\": true")) — Linus-style 'parse properly' alternative is deferred per F-LANE-SEAM-IMPL-FULL-JSON but never explicitly named as rejected in the changeset itself.

Hyperscaler-style alternatives (sharded scanning, event-stream emission, CI-matrix-per-canonical-home) are not considered in code or FixupTask body — only the single-process synchronous-scan design appears.

check_naming_convention caps violations at 10 (L792-794) — a sound choice for human-readable output, but the truncation policy itself is an alternative that isn't documented (e.g. 'why not emit all + paginate?').

check_scorecard_render and check_consensus_debate_evidence both scan two directories (evidence/multispectrum + evidence/per-change) with identical loop structure — the DRY alternative (helper fn) was not selected; acceptable for 4 sub-checks but a maintainability ceiling.

extract_string_field (L717-727) is hand-rolled because the kernel is std-only per render_report_json comment (L919) — this IS a Linus-style 'no dependencies' alternative selected, but the rejection of serde_json should be named in the doc-comment, not implicit.
uncertainty_areas: Whether the 'std-only kernel' constraint that motivates hand-rolled JSON was formally adopted as an ADR or is informal — if formal, the alternative-rejection is captured upstream; if informal, F6 risk increases.
Whether other lanes in the workspace use a different sub-check pattern (e.g. async, parallel scan) that would constitute a competing alternative the author should have named.
Whether the 10-violation truncation in check_naming_convention has a downstream consumer that depends on bounded output, or whether it's a UX-only choice.
alternatives_named: A: Day-1 stub + std-only scan + bounded FixupTask (THE SELECTED PATH — register F-LANE-* in fixuptasks.jsonl, surface NotYetArmed status, ship hand-rolled extractors).

B: Linus-style — pull in serde_json (kernel dep already justified by complexity), walk a real Cargo metadata DAG for the seam check, parse evidence JSON properly so the substring matches like raw.contains("\"meta_review_triggered\": true") cannot false-positive on string-literal contents.

C: Hyperscaler-style — shell out each sub-check to a sandboxed worker process, emit findings on an event-stream, run the four scans in parallel via std::thread::scope, and arm a CI matrix per canonical home (specs/, registries/, evidence/, templates/) so scaling violation-counts past the 10-cap is free.

D: Defer to external linters — outsource naming-convention to a pre-commit hook + check_naming_convention reads its output; outsource rust-default-language to cargo-deny / a workspace-level ripgrep config rather than re-implementing dir-scan in the lane crate.

E: Schema-driven dispatch — replace the four hand-written pub fn sub-checks with a single dispatcher that consumes specs/cross-cutting/multispectrum-review.json#scorecard_schema + a sub-check registry JSON, so adding a fifth sub-check is data, not code.
selected_rationale: Option A (the as-shipped path) is correct for Day-1 because: (1) the seam lane must stay std-only per the render_report_json kernel-dep policy, ruling out B's serde_json arm; (2) all four FixupTasks are properly registered with priority + reasoning, satisfying the F6 'bounded later' gate; (3) NotYetArmed status makes the deferral visible to CI and reviewers — silent regression is prevented; (4) the four sub-checks ship together, providing the surface needed to land subsequent FixupTasks incrementally; (5) Day-1 substring matching gives real signal (e.g. counts of meta-triggered evidence) even before full parsing.
rejected_reasons: B (Linus-style serde_json + Cargo metadata): rejected day-1 because adding serde_json to the seam kernel crate would violate the std-only constraint visible in render_report_json's hand-rolled emission. PROPERLY deferred via F-LANE-SEAM-IMPL-FULL-JSON. Acceptable rejection — but the rejection should be NAMED inline in the doc-comment for each sub-check, not only in extract_string_field.

C (Hyperscaler-style parallel + sharded + event-stream): rejected day-1 because the four sub-checks scan O(hundreds) of files in total — parallelism would be premature optimization. NOT properly deferred — no FixupTask exists for 'arm parallel scan when N>10k'; this is an acceptable omission but should at least be acknowledged as 'considered + deferred until throughput becomes a constraint'.

D (External linters / cargo-deny): rejected because the lane is the single source of truth per the seam-lane contract (it must emit one composite report). Splitting checks across pre-commit hooks would fragment evidence emission. CORRECTLY rejected — but again not named in code.

E (Schema-driven dispatcher): rejected day-1 because four sub-checks does not justify a meta-layer; the YAGNI threshold is correct. PROPERLY rejected by inaction — but if a fifth sub-check lands without revisiting this, E becomes a debt.
linus_style_alternative: Parse the workspace properly: use serde_json to read evidence/*.json into typed structs (EvidenceRecord { meta_review_triggered: bool, change_class_id: String, facets: Vec<Facet> }), walk Cargo.toml workspace metadata via `cargo_metadata` crate for the seam check, and replace extract_string_field with a typed accessor. Cost: 2 new deps (serde_json, cargo_metadata) in the kernel crate. Benefit: no false-positive risk from substring matching against string-literal contents (e.g. an evidence file that quotes 'meta_review_triggered: true' in a description field would currently false-positive in check_consensus_debate_evidence). This alternative IS captured as F-LANE-SEAM-IMPL-FULL-JSON in upstream FixupTasks but is not cited in the four new sub-checks' doc-comments.
hyperscaler_style_alternative: Treat each canonical home (scripts/, specs/cross-cutting, registries/cross-cutting, evidence/multispectrum, evidence/per-change, evidence/debate, templates) as a shard. Run the four sub-checks under std::thread::scope so all 7 directory walks complete in parallel; emit findings on an mpsc::channel and aggregate at the join point. For evidence at hyperscaler counts (>10k files), arm a CI matrix that splits scans across N runners by file-hash modulus and merges sub-check reports via render_report_json. Cost: complexity in run_composite. Benefit: scales to enterprise evidence-volume without re-architecting. NOT currently captured in any FixupTask — F6 recommends opening F-LANE-SEAM-PARALLEL-SCAN as a low-priority follow-up so the deferral is bounded.
